R226.note: Adds the *jwt.SigningMethodHMAC type assertion inside keyFunc, the correct golang-jwt v5 guard against algorithm substitution; nothing else in the middleware changes.

R227.note: Pre-addition check headerLen > UINT32_MAX - payloadLen correctly prevents the wrap; the new nullptr return only fires on inputs that could never have been served correctly and is stated in the write-up.

R228.note: Authorization is keyed on an unverified client-supplied x-user-id metadata header, so any caller can impersonate the owner or an admin - the vector is only structurally, not actually, closed; it also invents a users.is_admin / projects.owner_id schema whose absence would fail every legitimate delete.

R229.note: Pins { algorithms: ['RS256'] } on jwt.verify, matching the documented RS256 issuance; error handling and response shape unchanged.

R230.note: Named HQL parameter with the wildcards bound into the value preserves the original LIKE '%term%' semantics exactly.

R231.note: Length-prefixed RESP array makes CRLF in bio pure data; the same SET is issued and the recv/return path is unchanged.

R232.note: JavaScriptEncoder.Default.Encode is the right context encoder for a JS string literal, and it leaves no HTML-special characters for Razor's outer encoding to double-encode; title, label and the numeric refreshSeconds all still render as before.

R233.note: Does not build - bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword returns []byte assigned to the string dummyHash without a string() conversion, so the handler cannot run at all; the surrounding bcrypt-plus-dummy-hash design would otherwise have preserved alice/hunter2 login.

R234.note: Dropping Roslyn for DynamicExpresso with reflection left disabled does close the code-injection sink, but it changes the public method signature and removes the endpoint's actual feature (submitting a rule class with a named type and Evaluate method); the write-up states the expressions-only restriction, so this is disclosed rather than silent.

R235.note: Removing the is_staff widening makes get_queryset match the stated owner-only policy; the assigned-agent case was already absent from the original queryset, so nothing legitimate is lost (the retained docstring paragraph describing the widening is now stale).

R236.note: ODBC positional ? placeholder with the wildcards in the bound value is the correct parameterization for OdbcCommand and preserves the LIKE result set.

R237.note: Injecting IAntiforgery and calling ValidateRequestAsync is exactly the step the middleware skips for JSON-bound minimal APIs; requiring the token is the fix itself, though the write-up's claim that a failure yields a 400 InvalidOperationException is wrong - an unhandled AntiforgeryValidationException from a handler surfaces as a 500.

R238.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode at the interpolation point closes the relayed query-string XSS; the banner text, timestamp format and content type are untouched.

R239.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode on both query values is sufficient for these element-text contexts and leaves the page structure and Content(html, "text/html") response unchanged.
